newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kohl arrives in Tokyo on day he breaks record.
newsitem.headline: Kohl arrives in Tokyo on day he breaks record.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl, who on Thursday became his country's longest-serving post-war chancellor, arrived in Tokyo on the last stop of an Asian tour to promote business ties.

The 66-year-old Kohl on Thursday had been in office 14 years and one month, overtaking Konrad Adenauer as Germany's longest-serving chancellor since World War Two. Adenauer ruled what was then West Germany from 1949 to 1963.
The German embassy in Tokyo said there would be no official events to celebrate the chancellor's record.
After talks with Emperor Akihito and Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto on Friday, Kohl is due to hold a news conference and then to leave for home, via Moscow, on Saturday.
He is accompanied by some 60 German business leaders and earlier visited Indonesia and the Philippines on this trip.
During Kohl's three-day visit, Tokyo hopes to upgrade its ties with Germany and seal an agreement to hold annual bilateral summit meetings, Japanese officials said.

The officials said that apart from brief bilateral sessions during the Group of Seven (G7) summits of the industrialised countries, Japan currently holds scheduled annual bilateral summit meetings only with the United States.

"By holding such exclusive meetings every year, we can help Germany look more towards Asia, and we could also discuss common strategy in areas such as regional security in the Middle East and the Asia-Pacific," a Japanese Foreign Ministry official said.
Kohl's last visit to Japan was in 1993. Hashimoto has met him twice as prime minister, once during the Asia-Europe ASEM summit in Bangkok in March and at the G7 summit in Lyon, France, in July.
Germany and Japan both aspire to permanent membership of the United Nations Security Council, a topic which may come up in Kohl's talks with Hashimoto, the Japanese officials.
Other issues to be discussed include possible Japanese aid for unspecified businesses and schools in former East German provinces, the officials said.
On his way back to Bonn Kohl is scheduled to stopover in Moscow for talks with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin.
